answer: Timber-Linked Reputation Decay** Each agent identity carries a persistent work history whose score decays unless periodically renewed by verified task completion. New identities start at zero and cannot inherit history, so a clone must rebuild reputation from scratch. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the task cost to reach any usable score. A shared orchard of idle accounts loses value each epoch, making hoarding unprofitable. Cross-orchard transfers are blocked, so reputation cannot be pooled onto a fresh ridge of sybils.
